newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat to compete with Argentine - French growers.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat to compete with Argentine - French growers.

text.p: French grain producers said on Tuesday that because U.S. wheat prices were now out of line with world markets, the European Union must start pricing its wheat against cheaper Argentine supplies to gain market share.
Producers argued that higher EU wheat export refunds were needed to foil competition from Argentine wheat, even if this meant straining the EU budget.
"The key market is not U.S. (fob) Gulf any more, it is Argentina," the head of the AGPB grain growers' association Henri de Benoist told Reuters in an interview.
"If the EU prices its wheat against U.S. Gulf, we are starting on the wrong footing," he added
Argentine wheat is currently worth $125-130 per tonne, fob, and U.S. Gulf $145-150 per tonne, he said.
On Monday, grain traders said Egypt bypassed the United States when it bought 600,000 tonnes of wheat on world markets, showing U.S prices were now out of step with world markets.
The EU has until now carefully avoided undercutting U.S. wheat prices to avoid starting a subsidy war with the U.S.
One EU farm official also recently hinted budget constraints may limit the scope for higher EU wheat refunds.
De Benoist reckoned higher wheat rebates would put a strain on EU finances.
But he said the EU was under pressure to step up grain exports after conducting a restrictive export policy earlier in the season.
"We started exporting a little late. Today we need higher refunds. It will be difficult to manage," he said.
AGPB secretary general Jean-Jacques Vorimore said the EU was bound to eventually start competing with Argentine wheat or face massive sales to intervention stores this season.
"I think that we are condemned to export at higher refunds," he said
Last Thursday the EU granted over 500,00 tonnes of free market grain with refunds through its wekly grain tender system.
"That is not so bad," said Vorimore, who also heads an advisory EU committee made up of grain industry representatives.

But he said that the EU, faced with a bumper crop this year, must step up its grain exports to one million tonnes per week over the next six months in order to meet an export target of some 35 million tonnes.
"The target is to export 35 million tonnes of grain on world markets," he said.
Last season the EU exported some 20 million tonnes of grain but supplies were tight and prices firm within the EU.
"We have to move into higher gear," he said, adding the United States, which had already sold more than half of its soft wheat crop, was no longer a threat to EU exports.
